name: Mordecai
bio:
Mordecai, a Benjamite descended from Kish, had been carried into exile from Jerusalem with King Jeconiah. Living in Susa, he raised his orphaned cousin Hadassah, also called Esther, as his own daughter. When King Ahasuerus searched his empire for a new queen, Esther was among the young women brought to the palace; Mordecai instructed her not to reveal her Jewish identity, and he kept daily watch outside the harem to learn how she fared. After Esther became queen, Mordecai, now serving at the king's gate, overheard two chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, plotting to assassinate the king; he reported it through Esther, the plotters were hanged, and the event was recorded in the royal chronicles (Esther 2:5-23). His pivotal role opposing Haman is told in detail in the chapters ahead. When Haman was promoted above all other officials and demanded reverence, Mordecai alone refused to bow, revealing he was a Jew; Haman's fury at this led him to plot the destruction of all Jews in the empire (Esther 3:1-6).

 When Mordecai learned of Haman's decree, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourned bitterly in the city; through the chamberlain Hatach, he sent Esther a copy of the decree and urged her to plead with the king for her people. When Esther hesitated, fearing death for approaching the king unsummoned, Mordecai warned her that she would not escape the coming destruction either, and famously asked whether she had come to her royal position for exactly this moment; Esther then resolved to go to the king, risking her life, and asked Mordecai to have the Jews of Susa fast for her three days (Esther 4:1-17).
